AGREE.definition: Agree to, offer, promise, or otherwise indicate willingness or commitment to cooperate, including promises to sign or ratify agreements.
exemplars: Indicate willingness to cooperate in the future
Promise to sign a treaty
Expressing willingness to meet in the future
Invite a delegation to visit (note: this only includes invitations: actual visits/meetings do not fall under this definition)
Agree to cooperate in the future
Express willingness to end a conflict
notes: If two parties make a reciprocal agreement, code both as ACTOR (with no RECIPIENT)

CONSULT.definition: All consultations and meetings: this includes visiting and hosting visits, as well as meeting at a neutral location, and consultation by phone or other media.

modes.visit: a political actor visiting another actor, who is hosting
modes.third-party: A meeting between two actors is hosted by a third actor
modes.multilateral: A meeting that occurs in a multilateral context, typically an alliance or IGO
modes.phone: Consultation that occurs via phone or some other remote medium

notes: The visitor is the ACTOR; host is RECIPIENT
If two parties make a reciprocal agreement or have a meeting, code both as ACTOR (with no RECIPIENT)
If two parties make a reciprocal agreement, code both as ACTOR (with no RECIPIENT)

SUPPORT.definition: Any verbal support, verbal cooperation, approval, or finalizing a treaty or agreement. Note that this only includes verbal support. Material support or major concessions should be coded under COOPERATE, AID, or CONCEDE. This category only includes verbal support.
exemplars: express support for, commend
Initiate, resume, improve, or expand diplomatic cooperation
Approve policy, action, or actor
ratify, sign, or finalize an agreement or treaty
initiation of diplomatic ties with an entity for the first time.

CONCEDE.definition: Verbal concessions which have no immediate material consequences.
exemplars: Make a promise of future concessions
Make a promise of future easing administrative or legal restrictions on persons and organizations
Make a promise of removing curfews in the future
declarations (but not implementations) of ceasefires
promise to withdraw from territory (in the future)

COOPERATE.definition: Initiate, resume, improve, or expand mutual material cooperation or exchange. Note that this category excludes aid, which is primarily for the benefit of the recipient.
exemplars: Initiate, resume, improve, or expand economic exchange or cooperation
Military exchanges such as joint military games and maneuvers
Engage in cooperation on judicial matters, such as extraditions and war crimes.
Engage in voluntary exchanges or sharing of intelligence and other significant information.

AID.definition: All provisions of providing material aid whose material benefits primarily accrue to the recipient. (Activities for the benefits of both parties are defined as COOPERATION, not AID.
exemplars: Provide monetary aid and financial guarantees, grants, gifts and credit
Provide military and police assistance including arms and personnel.
Provide humanitarian aid such as emergency assistance.
Grant asylum, both to persons in its territories (territorial asylum) and diplomatic asylum on the premises of an embassy.
Provide debt forgiveness or loan cancellations
Rescue hostages

RETREAT.definition: RETREAT covers any events—not just military “retreat” from territory—which have immediate (not simply promised) material consequences. Promises of future actions do not fall under this category, only actions that have immediate consequences. This category differs from CONCEDE in that concessions are verbal concessions, while RETREAT relates to material concessions.

modes.disarm: Disarm militarily or give up weapons
modes.ceasefire: Implement ceasefire (note: this does not include a promise of future ceasefire, just the actual implementation of a ceasefire)
modes.access: Allow election observers into the country
modes.resign: A resignation by a government official

notes: NOTE: Promises of future retreats do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only retreats that are actually occurring/occurred count.
NOTE: Promises of future releases do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only releases that are actually occurring/occurred count.
NOTE: Promises of future returns do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only returns of property that are actually occurring/occurred count.
NOTE: Promises of future disarmaments do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only retreats that are actually occurring/occurred count.
NOTE: Promises of future ceasefires do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only ceasefires that are actually being implemented count.
NOTE: Promises of future permission to peacekeepers do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only peacekeeping operations that are actually being implemented count.
NOTE: Promises of future resignations do not apply and are coded under a separate event. Only resignations that have already happened count.

REQUEST.definition: All requests, demands, and orders. Requests, demands, and orders are less forceful than threats and potentially carry less serious repercussions

modes.assist: Make a request for diplomatic relations or exchange
modes.change: Make a request for changes in policy, government, or institutions
modes.yield: Make a request for the release of prisoners
modes.meet: Make a request for a meeting

notes: NOTE: Protests (including protests making requests) are coded under a separate PROTEST category. Protest DO NOT fall under this category.

ACCUSE.definition: ACCUSE covers a wide range of events, including any kind of accusation, disapproval or criticism, investigation, or legal accusation

modes.investigate: Any investigation, including commissions, grand juries, judicial or political

notes: NOTE: Protests (including protests expressing disapproval) are coded under a separate PROTEST category. Protests DO NOT fall under this category.

modes.change: reject a request for change in policy
modes.yield: reject a request to release prisoners or hostages
modes.meet: reject a request for a meeting

notes: The ACTOR is the entity making the rejection. The RECIPIENT is the target of the rejection

THREATEN.definition: All threats, coercive or forceful warnings with serious potential repercussions. Threats are generally verbal acts except for purely symbolic material actions such as having an unarmed group place a flag on some territory.

modes.restrict: threaten to restrict movement of people or goods, including boycotts, strikes, blockades, and curfews
modes.ban: Threaten to ban political activities of particular parties or individuals
modes.arrest: Threaten to arrest, detain, or imprison
modes.relations: Threaten to suspend relations or talks
modes.rights: Threaten to restrict civil rights such as speech, expression, and assembly
modes.expel: Threaten to expel diplomats, peacekeepers, NGOs, etc
modes.territory: Threaten to occupy, seize control of the whole or part of a territory

exemplars: All threats, coercive or forceful warnings with serious potential repercussions. Threats are generally verbal acts except for purely symbolic material actions such as having an unarmed group place a flag on some territory.

PROTEST.definition: All civilian demonstrations and other collective actions carried out as protests against the recipient.

modes.demo: Organized protest/demonstration. Distinct, continuous, and largely peaceful action directed toward members of a distinct ‘other’ group or government authorities
modes.riot: Violent riot. Distinct, continuous and violent action directed toward members of a distinct ‘other’ group or government authorities. The participants intend to cause physical injury and/or property damage
modes.strike: Labor strike. Members of an organization or union engage in the abandonment of work- places, either within specific sectors/industries or across sectors/industries
modes.boycott: The boycott of an activity, person, country, or organization via the withdrawal of commercial or social relations
modes.obstruct: Protest by obstructing passage or access to a particular locale

SANCTION.definition: All reductions in existing, routine, or cooperative relations

modes.convict: Find an entity or behavior guilty, unconstitutional
modes.expel: Permanently or temporarily expel an entity from a group, organization, political party, or country.
modes.withdraw: A country withdraws itself from an organization, treaty, or group
modes.discontinue: Curtail, decrease, break, or terminate diplomatic, commercial, or material ex- changes

MOBILIZE.definition: All military or police moves, deployments, activations, etc. that fall short of the actual use of force. Note that the *use* of forces does not fall under this definition.

modes.troops: Mobilize armed personnel or units (excluding police)
modes.police: Mobilize or increase readiness of police or security units
modes.militia: Mobilize or increase readiness of any militia or non-state entity with significant military capability

COERCE.definition: Repression, restrictions on rights, or coercive uses of power falling short of violence.

modes.seize: Police or other authorities executing a search
modes.restrict: Impose restrictions on political freedoms or movement
modes.censor: Censor, ban or restrict access to publications or other information
modes.curfew: Impose state of emergency or martial law
modes.cyber: Engage in cyber attacks and crime, including hacking, security breaches, website attacks

ASSAULT.definition: ASSAULT events are deliberate actions which can potentially result in substantial physical harm, including violence, battles, or assaults.

modes.beat: beating; physically assault by striking individuals or groups with one-off or repeated blows, typically administered manually or by blunt instrument
modes.assassinate: Targeted assassinations (both successful and attempted) with any weapon
modes.destroy: Destroy property, demolish as part of a conflict
modes.primitive: Attack someone with primitive weapons: fire, edged weapons, rocks, farm implements
modes.firearms: Use firearms, including fifles, pistols, light machine guns to attack someone.
modes.explosives: Use mines, IEDS, car bombs (excludes suicide attacks)
modes.suicide-attack: Use suicide attacks, both individual attacks and suicide car bombings
modes.aerial: Use any manned aerial vehicles, e.g. aircraft, helicopters to carry out an attack
modes.drone: Use unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), drones to carry out an attack
modes.heavy-weapons: Attack someone using heavy weapons, including artillery, rocket launchers, armored vehicles, tanks, and similar weapons
modes.crowd-control: Use "crowd control" weapons, including tear gas, water cannons, firing weapons in the air, lathi charges, etc.
modes.cleansing: Engage in mass expulsions or deportations
modes.massacre: Instances of mass killing or massacres
modes.unconventional: Use of chemical, biological, radiation, and nuclear weapons
